ms.report:
A. Output: Flutter SDK Alpha core client
What was delivered: a publishable Dart/Flutter package hydra_client@0.2.0 that wraps the hydra-node HTTP and WebSocket API with typed messages, exponential-backoff reconnection, sequence-aware sync, snapshot/history hint integration, a pluggable state store, and a single HydraHeadFacade entry point. Concrete pieces:
・Typed inbound messages (HydraGreetings, HydraTxValid, HydraTxInvalid, HydraServerSnapshot, HydraTimedServerOutput, HydraRawMessage) and typed client inputs (Init, Close, SafeClose, Contest, Fanout, NewTx, Recover, Decommit, SideLoadSnapshot).
・Reconnection: ReconnectingHydraSession + HydraReconnectPolicy with capped exponential backoff and a messages stream that survives reconnects.
・Back-pressure controls and seq-aware sync: SeqTracker, HydraSyncPolicy, optional GET /snapshot/last-seen fast-forward on detected sequence gaps.
・Pluggable layers: HydraStateStore / InMemoryHydraStateStore, HydraSigner interface, custom http.Client injection for TLS pinning.

Acceptance criteria: SDK core features implemented and functional on Android and iOS; integrates cleanly with hydra-node.
Evidence:
・Source: packages/hydra_client/lib/src
・Public API surface: packages/hydra_client/lib/hydra_client.dart
・Hydra operationId to Dart method mapping: docs/API_MAPPING.md

B. Output: Cross-platform micropayments sample app (Android + iOS)
What was delivered: example/hydra_demo is a Flutter sample app that connects to a hydra-node, opens / joins a Head, commits L1 UTxOs, runs two in-head micropayment scenarios (a Dice game and a Snake game where each interaction settles as an L2 transaction inside the open Head), and closes / fans out. Builds for Android, iOS, and Linux.
Acceptance criteria: Prototype integrates cleanly with hydra-node, wallets, and sample dApps; functional on Android and iOS.
Evidence:
・Sample app source: example/hydra_demo
・Android scaffold: example/hydra_demo/android
・iOS scaffold: example/hydra_demo/ios
・Android APK
